sources.entry: Unitree Robotics Go1 - A quadruped robot "dog" designed for agility, real-time obstacle avoidance, and smooth motion. It is well-suited for hobbyists, educational institutions, and light security tasks.

summary.name: Unitree Go1
summary.one_liner: Unitree Go1 is a lightweight consumer-level quadruped robot dog (about 12 kg) with 360-degree-style fisheye depth sensing, AI human recognition and a radio-based "accompany me" follow system, sold in Air, Pro and Edu versions.
use_cases: accompanying a person outdoors as a follow robot
educational programming with a quadruped robot
summary.what_it_does: The page describes a roughly 12 kg quadruped robot dog with a folded size of about 0.588 x 0.22 x 0.29 m and an adaptive load of about 3-5 kg. Its SSS super-sensing system uses fisheye binocular depth cameras plus fisheye AI sensing for obstacle detection and human recognition. The ISS intelligent accompaniment system uses patented wireless vector positioning so the robot follows a person from the side rather than requiring constant looking back. The page lists a top speed of about 17 km/h (approximate, speed-test figure) and a 16-core CPU plus 384-core GPU. The Pro and Edu models add Python and scientific programming interfaces, a foot-end force sensor, expansion ports and, on Edu, a 4G module and radar options.
notable: Fisheye binocular depth sensing with AI human recognition
Wireless vector positioning follow mode (ISS system) instead of camera-based following
Python programming interface on the Edu model
Listed at $2700 (Air) and $3500 (Pro); Edu priced on request
caveats: Depth sensing needs good lighting and textured obstacles; ultrasonic emitters can interfere
Follow positioning relies on radio and can lose the person when an obvious obstruction is between them
Prices exclude tax and freight; Edu model requires contacting sales
Actual speed is limited for safety below the 17 km/h peak figure; outdoor use advised in cool weather
